_doc: SAMPLE camera derived from camera_rig.json by proportion_samples.py; not the game rig. Fixed sprite camera (06_STYLE_ART.md section 3, 07 section 2.4). Orthographic, one pitch for every facing. The camera never moves between facings; the character turns on the spot. Scale rule: px_per_m_1x = char_height_px / (reference_height_m * cos(pitch_deg)), so a standing reference body seen at this pitch projects to char_height_px at 1x; the render is render_scale times larger, and pixelate.py reduces it by exactly render_scale. pitch_deg and char_height_px are open director decisions ([D] in 06; spec section 3 samples 30/35/40 and 40/48/56).
pitch_doc: degrees below horizontal; the same pitch as the game camera
reference_doc: average_m standing height (bodies/bodies.json); giant and slight bodies use the same px_per_m so a giant is taller on screen
frame_doc: square cell at 1x (64 for average; giant will need 72, a later decision)
pivot_doc: feet centre (world origin) in 1x cell pixels, x from the left, y from the top; the camera is aimed so the origin lands on this pixel. 8 px of headroom is left below the pivot because a foot nearer the camera projects up to 6 px below it at 35 degrees (measured on average_m, facings S, E, W)
distance_doc: orthographic, so distance only has to clear the body; it does not change scale

facings.order_doc: facing k turns the character k * step_deg counter-clockwise seen from above. S (k=0) faces the camera; SE (k=1) faces the camera turned towards screen right; N (k=4) shows the back. Names are screen directions with S = towards the viewer.
